mcqs.q: Prosthodontics is the dental specialty concerned with:
opts: Diagnosis, treatment planning, rehabilitation and maintenance of patients with missing teeth
The conclusions drawn at the end of a research study
The surgical removal of teeth and alveolar bone
The management of acute and chronic oral infection
mcqs.explain: Prosthodontics restores oral function, comfort, appearance and health using biocompatible substitutes.

mcqs.q: The three main branches of prosthodontics are:
mcqs.explain: Removable, fixed and maxillofacial prosthodontics are the three branches.

mcqs.q: Removable prosthodontics is concerned with substitutes that are:
opts: Readily removable from the mouth by the patient
mcqs.explain: Removable prostheses (complete/partial dentures) can be taken out and replaced at will.

mcqs.q: A patient with NO remaining natural teeth is described as:
mcqs.explain: Edentulous = without teeth; treated with a complete denture. Dentate/dentulous = teeth present.

mcqs.q: A partially edentulous space may be restored by all of the following EXCEPT:
mcqs.explain: A complete denture replaces the ENTIRE dentition of a jaw; partial spaces are restored by RPD, FPD or implant.

mcqs.q: A 'prosthesis' is defined as:
opts: An artificial replacement of an absent part of the human body
The art and science of making replacements
mcqs.explain: Prosthesis = the artificial replacement itself; prosthetics = the art/science of supplying them.

mcqs.q: A denture is:
opts: An artificial substitute for missing natural teeth and adjacent tissues
A cemented crown on a single tooth
mcqs.explain: A denture replaces missing natural teeth and their adjacent tissues.

mcqs.q: A fixed partial dental prosthesis (FPD) is one that is:
opts: Cemented to natural teeth, roots and/or implants
Removed and replaced by the patient at will
mcqs.explain: An FPD (bridge) is cemented and not patient-removable; an RPD is removable at will.

mcqs.q: A complete denture replaces:
opts: The entire dentition and associated structures of one jaw
mcqs.explain: A complete denture replaces the whole dentition and associated structures of the maxilla or mandible.

mcqs.q: The impression (intaglio) surface of a complete denture is the part that:
opts: Has its contour determined by the impression and faces the tissues
Is polished and shows the buccal/lingual tooth surfaces
mcqs.explain: Impression/intaglio surface is shaped by the impression and seats against the tissues.

mcqs.q: The occlusal surface of a denture is the portion that:
opts: Is polished on the cheek side
mcqs.explain: The occlusal surface contacts the opposing denture/teeth.

mcqs.q: Denture RETENTION is the resistance to movement of the denture:
opts: Away from its tissue foundation, especially vertically
On its foundation against lateral forces
mcqs.explain: Retention resists vertical dislodgement away from the tissues; stability resists lateral movement; support resists seating toward the tissues.

mcqs.q: Denture STABILITY is the resistance of a denture to:
opts: Movement on its foundation, especially to lateral (horizontal) forces
Vertical dislodgement away from the tissues
mcqs.explain: Stability resists horizontal/lateral movement on the tissue foundation.

mcqs.q: Denture SUPPORT is the quality that resists movement of the denture:
mcqs.explain: Support resists vertical seating forces toward the tissues; broad load distribution is the 'snowshoe effect'.

mcqs.q: The 'snowshoe effect' in complete dentures refers to:
opts: Distributing masticatory forces across all the resilient supporting tissues
Concentrating forces on a single point
The cooling of the denture base
mcqs.explain: Like a snowshoe, the denture spreads load broadly over the tissues, aiding support.

mcqs.q: Maxillofacial prosthodontics is the branch that:
opts: Replaces missing facial and jaw structures
Cements crowns and bridges to teeth or implants
Replaces teeth with prostheses the patient can remove
Treats diseases of the dental pulp
mcqs.explain: Examples include nasal, orbital and auricular prostheses.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of a maxillofacial prosthesis?
mcqs.explain: Nasal and orbital prostheses are the other two examples given.

mcqs.q: Fixed prosthodontics is concerned with:
opts: Crowns and bridges cemented to teeth or implants
Prostheses the patient can remove at will
mcqs.explain: The defining feature is that the prosthesis is cemented, not patient-removable.

mcqs.q: A patient in whom natural teeth are present in the mouth is described as:
mcqs.explain: Edentulous means without teeth; partially edentulous means one or more but not all teeth are missing.

mcqs.q: 'Partially edentulous' means a patient has:
opts: One or more but not all natural teeth missing
mcqs.explain: Such a space can be restored with an RPD, an FPD or an implant.

mcqs.q: 'Prosthetics' is best defined as:
opts: The art and science of supplying artificial replacements for missing parts of the human body
An artificial replacement of an absent part of the human body
An artificial substitute for missing natural teeth and adjacent tissues
The specialty concerned with the dental pulp
mcqs.explain: A PROSTHESIS is the replacement itself; PROSTHETICS is the art and science of supplying it.

mcqs.q: A 'partial denture' is defined as a prosthesis that:
opts: May be removable OR fixed, restoring some but not all of the natural teeth
Is always removable and replaces the whole dentition
Is always cemented and replaces the whole dentition
mcqs.explain: The term covers both the RPD and the FPD.

mcqs.q: The defining feature of a removable partial dental prosthesis is that it:
opts: Can be removed and replaced at will by the patient
Is cemented to natural teeth or implants
Replaces the entire dentition of an arch
mcqs.explain: It replaces some teeth in a partially dentate arch.

mcqs.q: A complete denture is defined as a removable dental prosthesis that replaces:
opts: The entire dentition and associated structures of the maxilla or mandible
One or more but not all of the natural teeth
Only the anterior teeth of an arch
mcqs.explain: A patient who is edentulous is treated with a complete denture.

mcqs.q: The POLISHED surface of a complete denture includes:
opts: The buccal and lingual surfaces of the teeth and the part of the base that is usually polished
The portion whose contour is determined by the impression
The portion that contacts the antagonist
mcqs.explain: The impression (intaglio) surface faces the tissues; the occlusal surface meets the antagonist.

mcqs.q: How many surfaces does a complete denture have, and what are they?
opts: Four — impression, polished, occlusal and incisal
mcqs.explain: Each has a distinct role: tissue fit, muscle contact and function against the opposing arch.

mcqs.q: Resistance to movement of a denture AWAY from its tissue foundation, especially vertically, defines:
mcqs.explain: Stability resists lateral forces, and support resists movement toward the tissues.

mcqs.q: Resistance to movement of a denture ON its tissue foundation, especially to lateral forces, defines:
mcqs.explain: Lateral or horizontal forces are what stability resists.

mcqs.q: Resistance to movement of a denture TOWARD the tissues defines:
mcqs.explain: Support is what the snowshoe effect underlies — broad coverage spreading load across resilient tissues.

mcqs.q: Prosthodontics, in its fuller definition, pertains to the diagnosis, treatment planning, rehabilitation and maintenance of:
opts: Oral function, comfort, appearance and health in patients with missing teeth
Only the appearance of the anterior teeth
Only the vertical dimension of occlusion
mcqs.explain: It achieves this using biocompatible substitutes.

mcqs.q: Which three ways may a partially edentulous space be restored?
opts: Removable partial denture, fixed partial denture, or implant
Removable partial denture, complete denture, or crown
mcqs.explain: The choice between them is the core treatment-planning decision in partial edentulism.

saqs.q: Define prosthodontics and name its three branches.
saqs.a: PROSTHODONTICS is the dental specialty concerned with the diagnosis, treatment planning, rehabilitation and maintenance of oral function, comfort, appearance and health in patients with missing or deficient teeth and/or maxillofacial tissues, using biocompatible substitutes. BRANCHES — removable, fixed and maxillofacial prosthodontics.

ans.text: The dental specialty concerned with the diagnosis, treatment planning, rehabilitation and maintenance of oral function, comfort, appearance and health in patients with missing or deficient teeth and/or maxillofacial tissues, using biocompatible substitutes.

saqs.q: Differentiate between edentulous, dentate, and partially edentulous, and give a treatment option for each partial space.
saqs.a: EDENTULOUS — no natural teeth present; treated with a complete denture. DENTATE (dentulous) — natural teeth present. PARTIALLY EDENTULOUS — one or more but not all teeth missing; restored with a removable partial denture (RPD), a fixed partial denture (FPD), or a dental implant.

saqs.q: Define: prosthesis, denture, and complete denture.
saqs.a: PROSTHESIS — an artificial replacement of an absent part of the human body. DENTURE — an artificial substitute for missing natural teeth and adjacent tissues. COMPLETE DENTURE — a removable prosthesis replacing the entire dentition and associated structures of the maxilla or mandible.

saqs.q: Name and describe the three surfaces of a complete denture.
saqs.a: IMPRESSION (intaglio) surface — contour determined by the impression; faces the tissues. POLISHED surface — the polished part of the base, including the buccal and lingual surfaces of the teeth. OCCLUSAL surface — the part contacting the opposing denture or teeth.

saqs.q: Compare denture retention, stability and support.
saqs.a: RETENTION resists movement AWAY from the tissue foundation, especially vertically. STABILITY resists movement ON the foundation, especially against lateral (horizontal) forces. SUPPORT resists movement TOWARD the tissues (vertical seating forces), aided by broad load distribution — the snowshoe effect.

saqs.q: Describe maxillofacial prosthodontics and give three examples of maxillofacial prostheses.
saqs.a: MAXILLOFACIAL PROSTHODONTICS is the branch that replaces missing facial and jaw structures, restoring missing extra-oral structures for both function and appearance. EXAMPLES — the NASAL, ORBITAL and AURICULAR (ear) prostheses.

ans.text: The branch of prosthodontics that replaces missing facial and jaw structures, restoring missing extra-oral structures for both function and appearance.

saqs.q: Define prosthetics and partial denture, and distinguish an RPD from an FPD.
saqs.a: PROSTHETICS is the art and science of supplying artificial replacements for missing body parts, whereas a PROSTHESIS is the replacement itself. A PARTIAL DENTURE is a removable OR fixed prosthesis restoring some but not all natural teeth and/or associated parts. RPD — replaces some teeth in a partially dentate arch and can be removed and replaced at will by the patient. FPD — CEMENTED to natural teeth, tooth roots and/or implants, so it is not patient-removable.
